pr_title: Apply default light profile only when light is toggled from off to on
pr_body:
Partially revert #45450. ## Breaking change When a light entity has a default profile associated, the default profile will only be applied for the `light.turn_on` service call when the light state is off or no data is sent with the service call. The transition attribute from the default profile in `light_profiles.csv` will also be applied when `light.turn_off` is called. ## Proposed change A default light profile should only be applied during the service call `light.turn` on in 3 scenarios: - The light state is changing from off to on - No data is being sent in the service call - The default profile is explicity specified in the service call As there is no seperate service for the light entity to change brightness, the expected result when a service call to `light.turn_on`, for a light that is presently on is to change the brightness. It should not affect the colour. Specific scenarios can be seen in the table. My argument against #45450: - The documentation explicity says the default profile will be applied when the light is turned-on. https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/light/#default-turn-on-values - This reverted functionality is intuitive. Referencing the Front-end UI, when I open the light entity lovelace card, I can change the color, brightness or white level individually. Specifically, if a group of lights all have different colours, I expect that if I change the brightness, the colour remains the same while the brightness is adjusted for each light to the new brightness. - It is likely that a small proportion of users use the light_profiles. Of them, an even smaller portion would likely raise an issue if this functionality was not working as expected. However, there are 3 seperate issues and multiple commenters on each of these issues. - I was not able to locate any issues where a user identified that they expected the default profile to be applied anytime the light.turn_on service call was issued (prior to the afformentioned PR). The default transition attribute will continute to be applied for all `light.turn_on` service calls. It will also be expanded to apply to `light.turn_off` service calls, as was intended in #45450. As a result, it will also apply to `light.toggle`. This is believed to be intuitive to the user. **All of functionality remains the same except for row 7.**
Service CallLight Entity StateCurrent New StateProposed New State
No data and the light current state matches the default profile ```yaml service: light.turn_on target: entity_id: light.a ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 255 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 255 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 255 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ```
```yaml state: off ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 255 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 255 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ```
Including a parameter, with the light current state matching the default profile. ```yaml service: light.turn_on target: entity_id: light.a data: brightness: 254 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 255 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 254 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 254 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ```
```yaml state: off ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 254 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 254 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ```
No data and the light current state does not match the default profile ```yaml service: light.turn_on target: entity_id: light.a ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 254 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 255 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 255 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ```
```yaml state: off ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 255 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 255 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ```
Including a parameter and the light current state does not match the default profile ```yaml service: light.turn_on target: entity_id: light.a data: brightness: 254 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 255 xy_color: 0.46, 0.409 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 254 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 254 xy_color: 0.46, 0.409 ```
```yaml state: off ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 254 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ``` ```yaml state: on brightness: 254 xy_color: 0.362, 0.37 ```
Default Light Profile ```csv id,x,y,brightness light.a,0.36079,0.37000,255 ``` Note: The previous state or attributes when the light entity is off is assumed to be the on state referenced in the row above. ## Type of change - [ ] Dependency upgrade - [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New integration (thank you!) - [ ] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration) - [X] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break) - [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests ## Additional information - This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #45979 #46053 #46314 - This PR is related to issue: #49002 - Link to documentation pull request: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/17513 ## Checklist - [X] The code change is tested and works locally. - [X] Local tests pass. **Your PR cannot be merged unless tests pass** - [X] There is no commented out code in this PR. - [X] I have followed the [development checklist][dev-checklist] - [X] The code has been formatted using Black (`black --fast homeassistant tests`) - [ ] Tests have been added to verify that the new code works. Once you do that we will be able to review and accept this pull request.

Thanks!
Tagging @Adminiuga as this is explicitly undoing their change and they should have an opportunity to review it.
Default profile may contain only transition attribute and that should be applied to light.turn_off service ?
So for the turn_off service it should filter out the rest of the profile attributes but the transition.

Would this also help me out with this issue https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/46314#issuecomment-786706132
which is still a very undesired side effect of the PR  #45450 ?

> Default profile may contain only transition attribute and that should be applied to light.turn_off service ?

That is not a documented feature. In fact, the documentation implies that a color must be specified.
https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/light/#default-turn-on-values

However, I can see how a default transition attribute could be useful for a light entity in general.
Perhaps there should be a seperate attribute that can be set for each light entity that will assign a default transition attribute. This would result in two seperate "defaults", which I could see useful application for:
- Light Turn-On Default (the pre- #45450 behaviour); applying as described in my PR.
- Light Transition Attribute Default, applying by default to all light.turn_on, light.turn_off, light.toggle, lifx.set_state etc; unless otherwise overwritten.

Is that what your intention is? I would make the argument that the transition attribute default should be a new feature, and that the light Turn-On Default should be reverted, as per this PR. Ideally these would both be configurable via the gui.

> Would this also help me out with this issue [#46314 (comment)](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/46314#issuecomment-786706132)
> which is still a very undesired side effect of the PR #45450 ?

Yes. Thats the whole reason I created this PR. Your issue is the functionality described in row 7 of the table.
this would be so very welcome! thanks for writing it indeed.

> So for the turn_off service it should filter out the rest of the profile attributes but the transition.

I'm debating in my head whether this is intuitive, and expected functionality. Perhaps an alternate course of action is to split the light profiles into three seperate functions or ideas.

For each light entity:
- The turn on default colour attribute is only applied as described in the PR. With the "default" profile, becoming an entity specific named profile.
- The default transition attribute is applied to all light.turn_on, light.turn_off, light.toggle, lifx.set_state etc; unless otherwise overwritten.

Light "Scenes":
- Named profiles with a colour.

I think I'm in agreement that the transition attribute should be applicable as-is for the current functionality.  I believe it intuitively make sense for users (the transition attribute).  One could make the argument that all light functions have a default transition attribute as-is, 0. This could be interpreted like some hardware dimmers function, having the same transition time regardless if you are turning the switch on or off. As-long as its explicitly documented, I think this might be a feasible option.

What am I proposing?
- Remove the "transition" attribute from named profiles, and add it as a configurable item for light entities.
- Is this feasible? How much work would be involved?: I don't know.

Seems like maybe it is better to have a turn_on_default profile, which is applied once only, for off to on transition. To me personally, default profile is a " default" which is always applied regardless of state. Users just shouldn't out all the attributes in the default profile.

Thoughts?

> Seems like maybe it is better to have a turn_on_default profile, which is applied once only, for off to on transition. To me personally, default profile is a " default" which is always applied regardless of state. Users just shouldn't out all the attributes in the default profile.
> 
> Thoughts?

I can't think of a use case where if I send a light.turn_on service call where I want to apply any attribute by default, except for the transition attribute. If I change the colour of a light entity, I dont want the brightness to change back to the default and 
vice-versa. If you can think of a common use-case, please let me know. 

Otherwise, I'm going to proceed with the following for each of the three attributes, and update the documentation accordingly:
- Brightness: as-specified in this PR.
- Color: as-specified in this PR.
- Transition: as described in my preceding comments for light.turn_on, light.turn_off, light.toggle.

I believe this would be relatively easy to program, while inconveniencing users the least. Unfortunately, I believe its out of the scope of this PR, and preceding issues to make the config more intuitive (aka seperate them into two seperate configs), besides using the documentation. Long term, I believe light profiles should be modified as follows, eventually eliminating light_profiles.csv:
- Deprecate/Eliminate named_profiles, with the potential to replace with custom named colors that can be called via color_name.
- Move the default transition attribute to the gui on a per light entity basis
- Move the default turn_on from power-off or no data specified (reset to default) to the gui on a per light basis

>  If I change the colour of a light entity, I dont want the brightness to change back to the default and
> vice-versa.

as suggested in my linked issue, I have tried to follow that advise, but it is fruitless and so counter intuitive. There's no way a household member accepts it to be normal to have the color change on changing the brightness or other way round. 

This new/changed behavior is unlike any real life usage we see on setting lights, other than on switching on maybe. Truly support this PR to re-iterate on that.

The PR has now been modified to match the intentions described in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/49376#issuecomment-822082918. Excluding adding new tests, its ready for review.

@Adminiuga can you confirm that you are in support of this PR now?

> Please make sure the tests pass as well.

Tests should pass now (they do locally), however, I am unable to run the workflow myself.

issue_context.title: Light Profile messed up
issue_context.body:
**The problem**

Since upgrading to 2021.2.0 the Light Profile has been screwed up.
Whenever I change the Brightness, it sets lights to the default hue or colour setting.
When I change the colour of the light globe, it will change the brightness to the "Default" brightness.

Example: When I set a light to 100% brightness, it will change the colour to a warm white (my default setting) even if the light is already on.   If I change the colour, it will change the brightness to 80% (my default brightness level when turning on a light) even if the light is already on.

Expected behaviour would be if the light is on and I change the colour, ,the brightness does not change to the default, but stays as it is set.  
Expected behaviour When the brightness of a globe that is already on is changed, the colour should remain as set and not change to the default colour 

**What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?**

2021.2.0

**What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?**

2021.1.5

**What type of installation are you running?**

Home Assistant OS

**Integration causing the issue**

Light / Light Profile

**Link to integration documentation on our website**

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/light/

**Example YAML snippet**

```yaml
# Put your YAML below this line

```


**Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?**

```txt
# Put your logs below this line

```


I have no traceback or YAML as this happens directly in the UI and no error log is actually created.
The default light profile changes seem to have caused this behaviour.

Seconding this issue, it seems that a related factor that is causing issues here is that the XY color value limitation injects white values into the requested color. Quite a few bulbs come stock (or through ESPHome or Tasmota settings) with firmware that doesn't like or specifically rejects mixing white values and color values. 

This only seems to occur for me if a specific default profile is defined in the light_profiles.csv I created, I'm not sure where the stock one is located. Austwhite, did you create a light_profiles.csv?

My understanding is that the toggle service already relies on the light.is_on state. It just process' the the service call to be a light.turn_on or light.turn_off appropriately.

That is not what I meant with this question. My question was on the transition itself.

This will call the off/on directly after each other. Now profile (and thus transition) becomes part of the turn off, does that mean it waits until the transition has been completed before turning it on again? Or?

If a light has a default transition of 5 seconds, it would be treated the same as if `light.toggle`, `light.turn_on` or `light.turn_off` was called with a transition of 5 seconds. In other words, for this same light, calling `light.turn_off` with a transition time of 5 seconds and `light.turn_off` without a specified transition time should both have identical results and behaviour.

Agreed, but not if called without a transition.

Assume this service, with a light that sets the transition to 5 seconds in its profile, the light if on before calling this service.

```yaml

  target:
    entity_id: light.example
  data: {}
```

- Turns on the light, using transition from profile

With this change:
- Turns off light, with a transition of 5 seconds...
- ?????
- Turns on the light, with a transition of 5 seconds

The ???? part is interesting and is definitely different now. What does happen there? Does this whole change take 10 seconds now? Or still 5?
